title: CROA Compiled Commitment (cc.*)
description: The immutable, content-addressed, signed execution commitment produced by the Contract Compiler (C7). It is the sole artifact authorized to cross the Execution Boundary. Normative source: CROA Standard Part II §4.4.1. In any discrepancy, Part II §4.4.1 prevails. (The Compiled Commitment was named 'RFC / Request for Change' in drafts prior to v1.0.0; it is unrelated to IETF RFCs.)

cc.id.description: Content hash (SHA-256 or stronger) over the canonical serialization of all other CC fields; the stable identifier.

cc.action.description: The grounded governed action (gga.*) received from C3, including the grounding record; gga.semantic_result MUST be GROUNDED (§4.5.1).

cc.subject.description: Authenticated subject identity for the session.

cc.permit_event_id.description: event.id of the C5 permit decision record.

cc.authorization_scope.description: The set of operations this CC authorizes against governed external systems; defines exec(r) in §6.2. NOTE (disambiguation, §4.4.1): this field is the *executable operation set* of the commitment. It is distinct from, and MUST NOT be conflated with, the governed-exception fields cc.auth_ref and cc.exception_scope, which reference and bound a C1 authorization artifact under PERMIT_WITH_AUTHORIZATION. A CC may carry cc.authorization_scope with no exception (ordinary PERMIT).

cc.decision_basis.description: The C2.eval permit output this CC was compiled from (§4.4.3). When PERMIT_WITH_AUTHORIZATION, cc.auth_ref and cc.exception_scope MUST be present; when PERMIT they MUST be absent.

cc.auth_ref.description: Present if and only if cc.decision_basis is PERMIT_WITH_AUTHORIZATION. The identifier (auth_id) of the single C1 authorization artifact (§4.3.1) under which this CC was compiled, bound in by C7 (§4.4.3). Binds the governed exception to this exact CC so the authorization is single-use and per-action: C6 MUST atomically redeem the referenced authorization at admission (§4.8), and MUST reject any second CC referencing an already-redeemed auth_ref (see NT-007, Appendix Q).

cc.exception_scope.description: Present if and only if cc.decision_basis is PERMIT_WITH_AUTHORIZATION. The bounded exception scope copied unchanged from the authorization artifact (§4.3.1) by C7 (§4.4.3): the specific invariant(s) waived, the single action class, target constraints, and validity window. C6 MUST enforce that the executed operation lies within this scope; C4 MUST deny any operation exceeding it (§4.3.1). It does not widen cc.authorization_scope.

waived_invariants.description: The specific registered invariant identifier(s) this exception waives — never a wildcard.

action_class.description: The single action class the exception covers.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC validity window end for the authorization; mandatory (§4.3.1, §2.5.1).

cc.policy_artifact_id.description: Identifier and version of the C1 policy artifact under which the permit was issued.

cc.invariant_set_version.description: Version of the enterprise invariant registry at compile time; C6 verifies consistency at execution time (§4.8).

cc.reversibility_class.description: Reversibility/consequence class (Part I, Tenet T5; Part II §4.4.1) of the governed transition this CC authorizes. R0 fully reversible; R1 compensatable; R2 irreversible low-impact; R3 irreversible high-impact; R4 irreversible critical. An unassigned transition MUST be recorded as at least R2.

cc.compensating_controls.description: For a transition of class R1 or above: the documented control(s) recorded in the CC per §2.5.1 and T5. Only R1 admits an actual compensation; for the irreversible classes the recorded control is preventive, not compensatory. R1: inverse/mitigating compensation path. R2 (irreversible, low-impact): the additional pre-execution authorization requirement T5 mandates beyond the standard permit decision (no inverse path exists). R3/R4: staged-execution, enhanced-evidence, C1-authorization, or human-approval conditions. Absent for R0.

cc.expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC expiry; C6 MUST NOT authorize any operation under a CC whose cc.expires_at is in the past.

cc.signer_id.description: Identifier of the C7 signing key used for cc.signature.

cc.signature.description: C7's signature over the canonical serialization of all other CC fields.

$comment: CCs are immutable; any content change yields a new cc.id and a new CC linked to the original. A CC missing any mandatory field is malformed and MUST be rejected by C6. cc.reversibility_class records the Tenet T5 R0-R4 class (Part II §4.4.1); cc.compensating_controls is required for R1 and above. cc.auth_ref + cc.exception_scope are present iff cc.decision_basis = PERMIT_WITH_AUTHORIZATION, and make the governed exception (§4.3.1) single-use and per-action, instantiable and boundary-enforceable (previously required only in prose §4.4.3).
